problem: LLM cascades use uncalibrated confidence scores requiring per-workload threshold tuning, causing a gap between theoretical promise and actual performance.
method: UCCI: calibration-first router that maps token-level margin uncertainty to per-query error probability via isotonic regression, selects escalation threshold by constrained cost minimization under three explicit assumptions (large-model cost > small-model cost, large-model accuracy invariant to routing, access to calibrated error probability).
key_assumptions: cℓ > cs (large model cost greater than small model cost)
fℓ achieves fixed accuracy αℓ on test distribution invariant to which queries are escalated
access to calibrated error probability ˆp(x) = g(u(x))
main_contribution: A calibration-first router for LLM cascades using isotonic regression to calibrate token-margin uncertainty to error probability, threshold selection via constrained cost minimization, theoretical optimality proof, and empirical demonstration of 31% inference cost reduction at same accuracy.
datasets: production named entity recognition workload of 75,000 labeled queries with 6 entity types
results: "UCCI cuts inference cost by 31% (95% CI: [27%, 35%]) at micro-F1 = 0.91 while reducing ECE from 0.12 to 0.03; outperforms entropy thresholding, split-conformal routing, and FrugalGPT-style learned threshold at the same operating point."
limitations: Assumption of large-model accuracy invariance to routing may not hold in other domains
Reliance on isotonic regression requiring a calibration set
Focus on structured JSON extraction may limit generalization to other NER formats
future_work: Replicate method on public NER benchmark (e.g., CoNLL-2003)
Test with different small/large model families
code_availability: not stated in abstract; no public repository found via GitHub search

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: UCCI focuses on LLM cascades using token-margin uncertainty and isotonic regression for structured prediction; the idea is broader, targeting any diverse set of models with post-hoc calibration of output probabilities and common thresholds across models.
